prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: international editorial article cover, horizontal 16:9. Create a sophisticated, airy hand-drawn illustration of an organization becoming more capable through reusable methods, quality checkpoints and retained experience. NO WORDS OR LETTERS ANYWHERE; the picture must work for both Chinese and English readers. Three connected professional activities form ONE flowing scene along a gentle upward looping ribbon. At the lower left, a small adult professional uses drafting tools to turn a loose sketch into a clear repeatable procedure on a large, simple blueprint surface (skills and method). At the front middle, another adult checks the resulting precise piece through a measuring frame or quality checkpoint with a subtle check mark (guardrails/standards). At the right, a third adult files the annotated result into an orderly open archive of a few matching records (memory/retained experience). The ribbon curves naturally from the archive back toward the blueprint at a visibly higher level, ending with one understated upward arrow, conveying feedback improving the method on each pass. The blueprint, inspection frame and archive should be illustrated physical objects integrated into the same scene, not boxed icons or a labeled infographic. Each character is secondary, engaged in a credible professional task; no hero, no expressive faces, no childish assembly. Mature international editorial line art, slightly irregular thin slate ink outlines, warm nearly-white background, ample negative space, restrained pale blue and sage-green accents, tiny sparse stipple shading. Clean, calm, light and intentional, like a refined hand-drawn magazine concept illustration. Objects and actions clearly visible even in a thumbnail. Use just three essential objects and three small simple adult figures. No furniture clutter, machinery detail, dramatic perspective, photorealistic materials, glossy 3D, gradients, decorative icons, standalone symbols, text, characters, numbers, labels, logos, diagrams, toy blocks, puzzles, shape-sorter, books, robots, brains, bulbs, bridges, cliffs, scenery or coffee. This is a real illustration of shared organizational practice with an ascending feedback loop, not text-based consulting graphics.
